record.original_question: Do the geodetic systems of Diophantine equations associated with K4, the Petersen graph, and the Hoffman-Singleton graph share a hidden common structure in the distribution of their variables that would make it possible to construct the corresponding system for generating every geodetic graph homeomorphic to the still-undiscovered Moore graph with k = 57, including that graph itself?

evidence.quote: 3. Does there exist any sort of hidden structure contained within the distribution of the variables of the geodetic system of Diophantine equations associated with K4, the Petersen graph, and the Hoffman-Singleton graph that is common to the three systems and allows to construct the system to generate the class of all geodetic graphs homeomorphic to the undiscovered Moore graph (k = 57) including itself?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A geodetic graph is a connected graph in which every pair of vertices is joined by a unique shortest path. The complete graph $K_4$, the Petersen graph (the unique 3-regular Moore graph of girth 5 on 10 vertices), and the Hoffman–Singleton graph (the unique 7-regular Moore graph of girth 5 on 50 vertices) are geodetic, and each can be encoded by an associated "geodetic system of Diophantine equations" whose nonnegative integer solutions parametrize the geodetic graphs homeomorphic to it (i.e., obtained by subdividing its edges with internal vertices, where the number of subdivisions on each edge is a variable of the system, subject to the geodetic constraints).

A hypothetical Moore graph of degree $k=57$ would be a 57-regular graph of girth 5 and diameter 2 on $57^2+1=3250$ vertices; its existence is a long-standing open problem.

Question: Does there exist a hidden common structural pattern in the distribution of variables across the geodetic systems of Diophantine equations associated with $K_4$, the Petersen graph, and the Hoffman–Singleton graph that, if identified, would allow one to write down explicitly the corresponding geodetic system of Diophantine equations whose solutions generate the class of all geodetic graphs homeomorphic to the (still undiscovered) Moore graph of degree 57, including that Moore graph itself?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of a Moore graph of degree 57 remains a famous open problem in graph theory (confirmed by recent surveys and notes, e.g., the Open Problem Garden entry and the 2022 note "Existence of a Moore graph of degree 57 is still open"). No common Diophantine framework spanning K4, Petersen, and Hoffman–Singleton that would yield the system for the degree-57 case appears to have been established in the literature.
